title: 576 - Using LLMs at Oxide | RFD | Oxide
summary: Oxide's internal policy on LLM use: encouraged as reader, researcher, editor, reviewer and programmer, but humans stay responsible, prose is not LLM-written, and mandates are rejected.

assertions.quote: LLMs are superlative at reading comprehension, able to process and meaningfully comprehend documents effectively instantly.

verdicts.note: Summarization and document QA are among the best-validated LLM strengths, though errors and omissions on long technical documents still occur.

assertions.quote: LLMs are infamous pleasers — and you may find that the breathless praise from an LLM is in fact more sycophancy than analysis.

verdicts.note: Sycophancy is a well-documented LLM failure mode in research and vendor reports, though newer models and prompting can reduce it.

assertions.quote: At best, writing from LLMs is hackneyed and cliché-ridden; at worst, it brims with tells that reveal that the prose is in fact automatically generated.

verdicts.note: Studies show readers rate text lower once they believe it is AI-written and LLM prose has detectable stylistic tells, but careful use can produce unremarkable prose and 'always clichéd' overstates it.

assertions.quote: We use Pangram at Oxide, and have found its false positive rate to be extremely low.

verdicts.note: Independent evaluations find Pangram among the most accurate detectors with low false positives on typical text, but detectors in general degrade on edited, short or non-native-English text.

assertions.quote: but that review should not be accepted as a human substitute.

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.

assertions.quote: This is especially valuable for code that is experimental or auxiliary or otherwise throwaway.

verdicts.note: Direction is well supported: greenfield, low-stakes work gets the biggest gains in studies and surveys. The specific multipliers are anecdote.

assertions.quote: LLM-generated code should not be reviewed by others if the responsible engineer has not themselves reviewed it.

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: Such decrees are absurd: they undermine the autonomy and mastery essential in our work.

verdicts.note: Reports of token-maxing and resentment support it, but some mandated rollouts (e.g. Shopify, Coinbase) report adoption gains; evidence is anecdotal either way.

assertions.quote: Note this isn’t as simple as disclosure of usage

verdicts.note: A norm about research and engineering practice rather than a testable claim.

assertions.quote: we do not want to become as gavage geese, being force-fed unnecessary complexity in hopes that an LLM will somehow spare us from asphyxiation.

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.
